headline: A first run that explains itself
items: A spectrum analyser. Select an input or an output and its third-octave picture appears above the filter table; the dashboard shows every enabled output at once. Tools > Spectrum Analyser (Cmd+Shift+A) opens the full view, with the raw FFT bins as well as the bands. It runs on the device, so it sees S/PDIF, ADAT and I2S sources the host never touches - and it only runs while something is watching it.
A Subharmonic Synthesizer, and auxiliary outputs that Control Surfaces can drive.
Dashboard filter cards sit in a grid. Choose Auto or one to three per row from the gear on any card.

A Getting Started wizard runs on a first launch. It has one job - installing the DSPi firmware on your Pico and confirming it came back running - and it hands you the console the moment that is done. Skippable in one click, and rerunnable from the Help menu.

Firmware Update now installs. Put a board into bootloader mode, or let the app restart the connected device into it, and Console writes the matching firmware and confirms the device came back running it.
Console ships the firmware it expects. The RP2040 and RP2350 images are bundled, so the app and the device can no longer drift apart.
A banner appears if a connected device is running a different firmware version, with a one-click update. It stays out of the way when the versions agree.
Betas can now be told apart. The device reports which beta it is running, so Console knows beta 3 from beta 2 and offers the right update.
A short tour of the main window is offered once, covering channels, the graph, filters, volume, and the difference between changing something and committing it. Esc leaves it at any point.
Specialist features now introduce themselves the first time you open them, one card each, rather than being explained up front when they would mean nothing.
A Help menu, with Getting Started, the tour, release notes and documentation.
